rv.q: The four women’s palpable chemistry and the brisk pace in which their individual stories are told ensure that audiences remain engaged and enthralled throughout the play’s two hours of often outrageous comedy and delightfully anachronistic references and actions.
It is raw, and dark and uplifting all at once in ways that very few commercial productions dare traverse, and for that reason, the themes throughout will remain timeless.

With an iconic discography full of clever lyrics, it was only a matter of time before her breadth of work made its way to the stage. Lo and behold, we were graced with Jagged Little Pill, which is the latest national tour to make a stop at DCPA.
JAGGED LITTLE PILL stands out as the first artistically and socially responsible integrated catalog musical.
JAGGED LITTLE PILL is half brilliant and half hackneyed, but there are moments when it is dizzyingly great.
It is a must see for fans of Morissette's music, and a should see for fans of musical theatre.
Thankfully, Morissette’s songs, a talented cast and Diane Paulus’s direction make that unpacking intriguing to watch – if a little exhausting.

“Jagged Little Pill” is a spectacular show, which utilizes its relevant, universal story to transcend the original album’s alternative youth appeal, solidifying its place among timely yet timeless Broadway musicals.
Recommend – seeing this show at least once while it is in town, if not a few times more.

It’s a testament to the creative minds who put this stunning production together that an album from the 90s can be so successfully transformed into an urgent and inspiring work of musical theatre that confronts so many issues we face today, and does so with such verve.
'Jagged Little Pill' is raw like a fresh wound, but it's also moving and thrilling.
What is most surprising about JAGGED LITTLE PILL is how well the songs, for the most part, fit into the story.
'Jagged Little Pill' has plenty going for it and the creative team deserves praise for making many unexpected and innovative creative choices.
"Jagged Little Pill" cleverly weaves Alanis Morissette’s songs into the story of the dysfunctional Healy family.

My personal distaste for the show style and some of the artistic choices aside, the power of the songs themselves and the gameness of the performers means the show remains entirely watchable if a bit disappointing for what could have been.
Though nothing else in Mirvish’s touring production of Jagged Little Pill touches those divine minutes, a handful of other numbers make smart use of Morissette’s tunes (co-written with Glen Ballard).
The experience can relate to anyone, of any age.
I think her catalogue is really lovely, and I think it's wasted in this musical...

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Alanis Morissette musical, praising its ambitious storytelling and strong performances while questioning whether the jukebox format fully works. Sound quality issues frustrate some reviewers.
